extracted.intended_audience: investigators preparing NIH/NIAID U01 grant applications (biomedical researchers)
extracted.subtask_description: A sample U01 (cooperative agreement) application showing required sections and substantive expectations for project summary, facilities/resources, equipment, resource sharing, animal use, authentication of reagents, biosketches, consortium arrangements, and foreign site justification for a biomedical research proposal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Follow FOA/application format instructions
rubrics_metrics.description: Always follow your funding opportunity's instructions for application format.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The sample may not reflect the latest format or rules; NIAID posts new samples periodically. Applicants must obey the specific FOA (e.g., RFA-AI-18-042) formatting and submission requirements rather than relying wholly on older samples.

rubrics_metrics.name: Project Summary/Abstract
rubrics_metrics.description: A concise summary that states the central hypothesis, main aims, the approach (e.g., computational model identification, in vitro testing, in vivo validation), and the overall significance of the proposed work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Must succinctly describe the problem, hypothesis, key methods, and expected contributions (e.g., mapping effector response space, testing emergent antibody combination behavior). Include enough detail to convey novelty and feasibility to reviewers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Project Narrative (public health relevance)
rubrics_metrics.description: A short lay description of the project that explains its relevance to public health (e.g., understanding how antibodies influence each other in target cell killing when present together).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep it brief and accessible to a non-technical audience; state the potential impact on human health or disease therapy development.

rubrics_metrics.name: Facilities & Other Resources — Laboratory Space
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe dedicated laboratory space (square footage), specialized rooms (e.g., positive-pressure cell culture room), HVAC/electrical/service accommodations, and proximity to shared resources.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain how the physical lab setup and recent renovations are specifically tailored to the proposed work and how space supports experimental aims. Include access to bench/hood utilities, deionized water, and any dedicated equipment in that space.

rubrics_metrics.name: Facilities & Other Resources — Computational Resources
rubrics_metrics.description: List computing assets (e.g., office/workstation computers, lab servers, access to campus clusters like Hoffman2, network-attached storage, off-site backups).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document capacity for computationally intensive jobs (cores, memory, storage), software availability (MATLAB, development tools), backup/versioning procedures, and how these resources support data handling and analysis for the project.

rubrics_metrics.name: Facilities & Other Resources — Office and Administrative Support
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe office space for PI and lab members, departmental/college administrative support (funds management, purchasing, student advisement), and opportunities for formal mentorship and career development.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include details on desks, network access, filing, and institutional processes that ensure the research team can formulate experiments, analyze results, and prepare manuscripts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Facilities & Other Resources — Scientific Environment & Intellectual Rapport
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe the broader scientific environment: seminars, collaborative meetings, interdepartmental synergies, and regular joint meetings with collaborators that contribute to project success.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain how the environment and interactions (e.g., membership in cancer center, seminar series) increase probability of success through intellectual exchange, feedback, and access to expertise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Shared/Core Resources Access
rubrics_metrics.description: Document access to institutional core facilities (e.g., flow cytometry, genomics, imaging, high-throughput sequencing, biostatistics) and any discounted rates available via center membership.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: List specific core capabilities and relevant instruments; justify access and describe how core services will be used to complete proposed aims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equipment — In-lab and Shared
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide inventories of laboratory equipment available in the lab and via shared cores (e.g., centrifuges, thermocycler, –80°C freezer, NanoDrop, Incucyte live-cell imaging, confocal microscopes, flow cytometers, FACS Aria cell sorters, Mass Cytometer, plate readers).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Show that necessary instruments are available, functioning, and sufficient for proposed experiments (include brand/model when relevant). Indicate which equipment is shared and any arrangements/discounts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research & Related Other Project Information — Regulatory/Compliance Disclosures
rubrics_metrics.description: State whether human subjects are involved, vertebrate animals used, proprietary information included, environmental impact, historic place designation, and international collaboration details.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide IRB/IACUC status (pending/approved), Animal Welfare Assurance numbers, identify countries involved for international collaborations, and answer environmental/historic site questions per application requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Foreign Site Justification
rubrics_metrics.description: Explain why an international collaborator/site is included and how they bring unique, vital expertise or capabilities not available domestically (e.g., unique immunology expertise, experimental methods, in vivo models).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Demonstrate that the foreign site is essential to accomplish objectives and that inclusion furthers NIH goals more effectively than domestic alternatives. Describe the specific contributions of the foreign PI and lab.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consortium/Contractual Arrangements
rubrics_metrics.description: Confirm institutional awareness of the agency's consortium agreement policy and readiness to establish necessary inter-organizational agreements consistent with that policy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document administrative and programmatic personnel who will manage consortium relationships and ensure compliance with policies and agreements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multiple PD/PI Leadership Plan
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe leadership roles and responsibilities for multiple PIs, plan for continuity (e.g., replacement PI recruitment if a PI cannot perform duties), and assignment of administrative communications with NIH.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clarify primary responsibilities (e.g., one PI responsible for modeling and data analysis), communication channels with NIH, and contingency plans for PI departure or incapacity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resource Sharing Plan(s)
rubrics_metrics.description: Commit to sharing research outputs: publications (PubMed Central/open-access), raw data, reagents (plasmids via AddGene), mass spectrometry data (PRIDE), analysis source code, and other raw data deposited in appropriate repositories (e.g., ImmPort).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specify repositories and timing (e.g., make source code and analysis pipeline publicly available on or before publication). State anticipated resource types (no model organisms or GWAS in this study) and how sharing will be implemented.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authentication of Key Biological and/or Chemical Resources — General
rubrics_metrics.description: Use standard laboratory agents from established commercial sources and document provenance and validation procedures for reagents and materials.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State vendors and quality controls; maintain records and describe procedures that ensure reagent reliability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authentication — Cell Lines
rubrics_metrics.description: Perform short-tandem repeat (STR) assessments regularly (at least annually) to ensure provenance of each cell line; perform mycoplasma testing at least every six months.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make STR and mycoplasma test results a routine part of experimental records to ensure reproducibility and validity of cell-based experiments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authentication — Receptor/Protein Expression Quantification
rubrics_metrics.description: Verify stable FcγR expression by quantifying absolute abundance using staining (FITC-coupled Abs against specific receptors) and comparison to beads with defined antibody binding sites in each experiment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include the specific clones and detection approach, and perform quantitation prior to binding experiments to ensure consistency across cell lines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authentication — IgG Glycosylation and Batch Consistency
rubrics_metrics.description: Verify IgG glycosylation profiles using MALDI-TOF analysis to (1) confirm no qualitative inter-batch changes and (2) confirm expected changes after enzymatic treatments (EndoS, PNGaseF).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Perform these analyses routinely when generating IgG reagents and document results as part of resource records.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authentication — Complex Formation Verification
rubrics_metrics.description: Validate formation and expected valency differences of TNP-IgG complexes by polyethylene glycol (PEG 6000) precipitation to observe qualitative differences in molecular weight among complexes and free IgG.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use established precipitation and characterization methods to confirm reagent preparation prior to functional assays.

rubrics_metrics.name: Antibody Handling and Documentation
rubrics_metrics.description: Aliquot antibodies upon receipt, store long-term at –80°C, and log lot numbers for all antibodies used. Use matched knockout or antigen-absent controls where noted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain detailed records of lot numbers and storage conditions to support reproducibility and troubleshooting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data Analysis and Archive
rubrics_metrics.description: Back up raw and processed data in a versioned manner on network-attached storage with off-site backup; store in-house analysis routines under version control and document the entire analysis pipeline from raw data to analysis products.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure permanent record of modified data, use version control for code, and plan public release of source code and analysis pipelines with or before publication to enable reproducibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Animal (Mouse) Resource Authentication and Husbandry
rubrics_metrics.description: Use previously characterized transgenic mouse lines with genotyping and transgene expression monitoring via PCR, in situ hybridization, and immunohistochemistry; continuously backcross to C57BL/6 to maintain genetic stability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cryopreserve sperm of non-commercial lines for rederivation if necessary; ear-tag mice and maintain printed genotype records for each identified mouse. Use professional animal facility housing and procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Biosketch Content and Organization
rubrics_metrics.description: Include a Personal Statement describing relevant background and role, Education/Training, Positions and Honors, Contributions to Science with selected publications, and other professional activities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the biosketch to highlight experience directly relevant to the proposed project, key publications (with PMCID/PMID where possible), mentoring history, and demonstrated ability to lead collaborative projects.
